limitations: Compliance with screening was only 58.2 percent
The higher crude incidence in the screened arm points to over-diagnosis, which the authors acknowledge
The authors estimate a lead time of about 0.5 years
critique: Factories, schools and enterprises were allocated as clusters. The mortality analysis did not adjust for within-cluster correlation, so the reported confidence interval may be too narrow. The magnitude of this effect cannot be recovered from the aggregate event counts alone.

384 of the 9,757 people allocated to screening were removed after randomisation because they refused, so the analysis is not intention to treat despite the paper's claim, and every exclusion is on the intervention side

Only HCC deaths were counted and all-cause mortality was never reported, so neither harm from screening and the surgery it leads to nor misattribution of cause of death can be excluded, and the standard safeguard against disease-specific mortality bias is absent
Crude HCC incidence was higher in the screened arm. Earlier detection and overdiagnosis can both increase recorded incidence during follow-up. The trial did not separate their contributions.

Survival measured from diagnosis is susceptible to lead-time bias because screening brings diagnosis forward. The authors estimated a lead time of about half a year. HCC mortality from study entry is a separate endpoint.

The trial enrolled Shanghai residents aged 35–59 with hepatitis B or a history of chronic hepatitis. Cirrhosis was not required. Applicability to a contemporary cirrhosis cohort is therefore limited. NCCN HCC v2.2026 (HCC-1) recommends ultrasound plus AFP every 6 months for eligible patients.

In Table 2, 46.5% of screen-detected cases received resection, 32.6% TACE or percutaneous ethanol injection, and 20.9% conservative care. This pre-BCLC treatment setting differs from current practice with transplantation and thermal ablation available.

The paper's own figures disagree: the narrative gives the stage III split as 22 (25.6 percent) against 45 (62.9 percent) while the table gives 22 against 42 (62.7 percent), and resection in controls is 5 (7.5 percent) in the table against 7.8 percent in the text
Compliance of 58.2 percent means that the measured effect is that of offering screening to a workplace population, and the paper presents no per-protocol or compliance-adjusted estimate alongside it
15042359.n: 18,816 people aged 35 to 59 with serological evidence of hepatitis B infection or a history of chronic hepatitis, recruited from more than 300 factories, enterprises and schools in urban Shanghai between January 1993 and December 1995 and cluster-allocated to 6-monthly alpha-fetoprotein and ultrasound screening (9,757 allocated, 9,373 analysed) or no screening (9,443); cirrhosis was neither required nor excluded
15042359.bottom_line: The Shanghai cluster-randomised trial compared 6-monthly ultrasound plus AFP with usual care in people at increased HCC risk. HCC mortality was 83.2 vs 131.5 per 100,000 person-years (37% relative reduction). The analysis did not account for clustering, 384 people who declined screening were excluded after allocation, and all-cause mortality was not reported.
15042359.funding: No funding statement; the trial predates registries and has no registration number

limitations: Post-randomisation exclusion occurred in 19 of 90 patients assigned to ablation, all of whom withdrew consent and chose resection; the authors state they do not think this affected the results
Mean follow-up was only just beyond 2 years, and the authors state they do not expect a difference with longer follow-up
The sample size was relatively small, and the authors argue a larger sample would not have changed the result because the curves were almost identical
critique: The ablation strategy included CT at four weeks and repeat ablation or ethanol injection for viable residual tumour. The reported final response includes these additional procedures.

The intention-to-treat analysis correctly retains all 90 patients assigned to ablation, including 19 who instead had resection. This crossover reduces the distinction between the assigned treatments. The abstract reports a separate comparison of 71 versus 90 after excluding the 19 crossovers.

All 19 patients who declined their assigned treatment crossed from ablation to surgery. The authors describe central computer-generated randomisation. The report gives limited information about allocation concealment, blinding or independent endpoint review. The direction of crossover alone cannot establish a failure of concealment.

The paper reports nonsignificant survival differences. Its adjusted Cox model gives P = 0.8414 for treatment group (Table 2). It gives no hazard ratio or confidence interval for the primary between-arm survival comparison.

Table 2 gives signed regression coefficients and P values. Albumin was the only significant survival predictor (P = 0.0018). The paper does not give hazard ratios, confidence intervals or the death count used for this model, limiting assessment of precision.

Four-year survival was the longest time point reported, whereas mean follow-up was 27.9 and 29.2 months. The late survival estimates therefore require caution, particularly given the absence of confidence intervals for the treatment difference.

The morbidity comparison sets 50 of 90 resections against 3 of 71 ablations, mixing the two different analysis populations in one sentence, and 46 of the 50 surgical events are moderate-to-severe ascites (27) or jaundice beyond 30 days (19) counted as major complications with no validated grading system

Adverse events were recorded. Three patients had mild skin burns and eight had fever after percutaneous treatment. The surgery group had a different pattern of complications. The report does not establish that event ascertainment was systematically different between arms.

Complete necrosis on CT was 62.0% after one percutaneous treatment and 91.5% after additional ablation or ethanol injection in 21 patients. Two patients received TACE for residual tumour. The survival analysis therefore compares treatment strategies that could require additional procedures.

A single device was used (RF 2000 with a 3.5 cm LeVeen expandable electrode) with the endpoint of a hyperechoic cloud larger than the tumour on ultrasound and no margin requirement, which is not an adequate technique for tumours approaching 5 cm, and 34 of 71 ablated tumours measured 3.1 to 5 cm

Diagnosis could be made by imaging and AFP above 400 ng/mL or by cytology or histology when those criteria were absent. Resection identified one case of focal nodular hyperplasia, and laparotomy identified disseminated disease in two patients. Surgical staging could detect disease that might be missed in the percutaneous arm.

The stated sample size calculation specifies an alpha risk of 0.05 and a beta risk of 0.8, which is the power rather than the beta risk, and the trial was powered on 2-year recurrence rather than on survival, so the survival conclusion that the paper advertises was never the question the design could answer
The 3 cm and 3.1 to 5 cm subgroup analyses involve 37 and 34 ablation patients and are reported as non-significant with no estimates, confidence intervals or interaction tests given

The comparator is open surgery as practised in one Chinese centre in 1999 to 2004, with a right subcostal incision, routine Pringle manoeuvre in 10 and 5 minute cycles and a mean 19.7-day hospital stay against 9.2 days, so the length-of-stay and analgesia advantages do not transfer to a laparoscopic era

The authors answer each of their three stated limitations by assuming the null they are defending, arguing in turn that the exclusions, the short follow-up and the small sample would not have changed a result whose curves were already superimposed
16495695.n: 180 patients with a solitary HCC of 5 cm or less randomised at one Guangzhou centre between November 1999 and June 2004, drawn from 3,775 patients with HCC hospitalised there; 90 to percutaneous ablation (of whom only 71 received it) and 90 to resection
16495695.bottom_line: Chen randomised 180 patients with solitary HCC no larger than 5 cm to percutaneous ablation or resection. By assigned arm, four-year overall survival was 65.9% versus 64.0% and disease-free survival was 48.2% versus 51.6%, without a significant difference. The abstract’s 67.9% versus 64.0% and 46.4% versus 51.6% exclude 19 ablation-arm patients who chose resection. Imaging complete necrosis rose from 62.0% after one ablation to 91.5% after repeat local treatment. The paper gives no treatment-effect hazard ratio or confidence interval.
16495695.funding: Supported by a grant from the Sciences and Technology Committee of Guangdong Province, China, 2002; no conflict-of-interest statement appears in the article

limitations: The comparison with surgery is historical, drawn from three surgical series, and the authors acknowledge the well-known limitations of historical comparison
Fourteen of 232 eligible patients (6.0 percent) could not be treated because the tumour was poorly visible on ultrasound or lay next to bowel or main bile ducts
Three of the treatment failures occurred next to a large vessel, which the authors attribute to heat loss in the ablation zone
The authors state that a randomised trial of ablation against resection below 2 cm would need a very large sample and is probably not feasible

The authors concede that the high overall recurrence rate shows it is the natural history of the cirrhotic liver, not the first treatment, that governs prognosis, and that all published survival curves reflect repeated multimodal treatment
critique: Five-year overall survival was 68% for the 100 patients the authors classified as potentially operable and 55% in the entire cohort. Comparison with surgical series requires the same patient-selection criteria.

The authors defined potential operability using age <75 years, ALT <3 times normal and bilirubin <1.5 mg/dL or absence of portal hypertension. The adjusted association of potential operability with survival was imprecise (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.31–1.26, p=0.192).

Three different complete-response figures appear in the same paper: 216 of 218 (97.2 percent) in the abstract, 214 of 218 (98.1 percent) complete radiological necrosis in the Results and 212 of 218 (97.2 percent) sustained complete local response; 216 of 218 is 99.1 percent, so the abstract's numerator and percentage do not correspond

The classification boundary creates the result: enhancement within the ablation zone or up to 2.0 cm from its border is local recurrence, anything beyond 2.0 cm is a new lesion, which yields a 0.9 percent local recurrence rate in a cohort where 80 percent of patients recurred somewhere in the liver

Disease-free survival of 26 percent at 3 years and 20 percent at 5 years is computed on 82 patients rather than 218, and the paper never states which 82 or why, while quoting confidence intervals as wide as 7 to 36 percent

The 14 patients excluded for poor ultrasound visibility or a high-risk location are precisely the tumours in which ablation fails and resection is straightforward, so the local-control endpoint is measured on ground selected to favour the technique; the paper also states that 218 of 232 is 93.3 percent when it is 94.0 percent

Technique was not standardised in any respect: five departments used at least four different electrode systems, including a 1.5 cm laterally deployed spiral, with power and exposure left to manufacturer recommendation and operator preference, and adequacy was judged by the extent of a hyperechoic cloud rather than by a measured margin on post-treatment imaging
Of 212 sustained complete local responses, three had explant confirmation. The other 209 were assessed on follow-up imaging, scheduled every 4–6 months.

Patients with any prospect of transplantation were excluded by design, so the cohort systematically omits the patients in whom the choice between ablation and resection carries the greatest consequence, and the authors justify this by Italian organ scarcity rather than by the clinical question

The only significant multivariable predictor of survival is the appearance of new lesions during follow-up (HR 1.97, 1.13 to 3.5), a post-treatment event entered as a predictor of a survival time it partly determines, and alpha-fetoprotein could not be analysed at all because only 11 patients had raised values, so the model contains no measure of tumour biology
Median follow-up was 31 months (range 6–134 months). Patients with shorter observation contributed less information to the 3- and 5-year survival estimates.

The surgical mortality the paper contrasts with its own 0 percent is a literature mean of 5 percent spanning 0 to 15 percent across series from different decades and countries, while the Italian hepatitis C surveillance population here (83.9 percent HCV, mean age 68, 44 percent female, 21.5 percent over 75) is compared with Japanese surgical cohorts

One of the four major complications is hyperbilirubinaemia lasting a month, and one is neoplastic seeding, so the 1.8 percent figure that anchors the safety argument contains a tumour implant from the procedure itself

The paper concludes that ablation should be the treatment of choice even when resection is possible, a statement of superiority drawn from an uncontrolled cohort by authors who in the same Discussion declare the controlled test of it unfeasible
18008357.n: 218 of 232 eligible patients with a single HCC of 2.0 cm or less and Child-Pugh A cirrhosis, treated by percutaneous radiofrequency ablation at 5 Italian departments between October 1995 and June 2006; the authors classified 100 as potentially operable
18008357.bottom_line: A multicentre cohort showing that radiofrequency ablation of a single HCC of 2 cm or less achieves sustained complete local response in 97.2 percent with no mortality and a 1.8 percent major complication rate. The 68 percent 5-year survival used to argue that ablation can replace resection belongs to the subgroup of 100 patients the authors classified as potentially operable, not to the cohort, whose 5-year survival was 55 percent with 80 percent recurrence and 20 percent disease-free survival; there is no control group and the authors argue the randomised trial that would settle it is not feasible.
18008357.funding: No funding statement appears; the authors declare no potential conflict of interest

limitations: The number of patients required to show superiority was underestimated because conventional chemoembolisation achieved a 44 percent response rate against the assumed 35 percent, which the authors state
Robust time-to-progression and survival data would require further randomised trials with longer follow-up, as the authors acknowledge
critique: Conventional TACE varies across centres in drug, dose, embolic agent and schedule. The study comparison applies to the conventional regimen used in this trial.

The bead protocol used 150 mg doxorubicin per session, whereas conventional TACE used 50–75 mg/m² with dose adjustment. The mean total dose was about one-third higher with beads (295 vs 223 mg). The trial compares these treatment regimens and cannot isolate the delivery platform from dose.

The modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded 9/102 bead recipients and 2/110 controls who never received TACE. Differential exclusion may favour the bead arm, although its direction cannot be determined from these data.

The three-stage design used one-sided α=0.025 and a final significance boundary of 0.02396. The observed one-sided p=0.11 did not meet this boundary. The trial enrolled 212 patients against a design of approximately 200.

Every analysis other than the failed primary endpoint and the primary safety endpoint is described in the Methods as supportive in nature and analysed descriptively, so all the positive statements in the paper are descriptive

The subgroup of more advanced patients (Child-Pugh B, ECOG 1, bilobar or recurrent disease) is described in the Methods as preplanned and in the Results and Discussion as post hoc and hypothesis-generating, with p values unadjusted for multiplicity; this subgroup is the basis for the paper's conclusion that the device offers benefit in more advanced disease

Thirteen patients with bilobar disease received a second embolisation of the other lobe within three weeks as procedure 1B, unevenly distributed (8 bead against 5 control), so treatment intensity differed between arms outside the randomised comparison

The primary endpoint is EASL radiological response at 6 months, a surrogate with no established relation to survival in this setting, and follow-up stopped at 6 months, so the trial cannot answer whether the device changes any outcome a patient would notice

Of 201 treated patients, 67 discontinued treatment, including 13 downstaged to curative therapy (5 bead, 8 control). Last observation carried forward was used for missing response measurements. The 6-month estimate therefore depends partly on earlier scans.

The control arm's embolic agent was left to investigator choice while the experimental arm used a single standardised device, so the comparison is between a defined product and a heterogeneous practice
The trial was sponsored by the manufacturer of the device under test, and the paper offers no statement about who performed the analysis or who drafted the manuscript

The later PRECISION Italia randomised trial (Golfieri et al.) reported no declared conflicts of interest. It found no significant difference in response, median time to progression (9 months in both arms) or 2-year survival (56.8% vs 55.4%, p=0.949), and stopped for futility.
19908093.n: 212 patients with Child-Pugh A or B cirrhosis and large or multinodular unresectable N0 M0 HCC randomised at European centres to drug-eluting bead chemoembolisation (102) or conventional chemoembolisation (110); the modified intention-to-treat population analysed was 93 and 108 patients who received at least one treatment
19908093.bottom_line: PRECISION V is the trial routinely cited as establishing drug-eluting beads, and it failed its primary endpoint: EASL objective response at 6 months did not differ significantly from conventional chemoembolisation. It is a phase 2 study with a six-month radiological endpoint, no time-to-progression or survival data, a fixed 150 mg doxorubicin dose in the experimental arm against a body-surface-area and bilirubin-adjusted dose in the control arm, and manufacturer sponsorship.
19908093.funding: Sponsored by Biocompatibles UK Ltd, the manufacturer of the DC Bead device under test, as declared in the acknowledgments

limitations: Enrolment was stopped for futility on the recommendation of an external review committee after the second interim analysis, at 177 of 214 planned patients

The power calculation assumed a 40 percent 2-year survival with conventional chemoembolisation and a 20 percentage point absolute gain with beads, which the authors concede was an optimistic view based on the device's theoretical advantages

Patients could receive ablation, resection, sorafenib or transplantation after chemoembolisation. The paper reports 36 of 177 receiving subsequent treatment in the Results and gives 26 in its discussion of limitations. The two counts are not reconciled.
The authors note the inclusion of BCLC C patients in whom chemoembolisation is debatable

The study permitted CT or MRI and used EASL response criteria until 2010 and modified RECIST thereafter. The investigators noted that retained lipiodol can obscure enhancement on CT after conventional TACE.
critique: At one month the control arm achieved a significantly higher overall complete response than the beads (59.8 against 43.8 percent, p = 0.036), and the authors explain this as a spurious effect of lipiodol masking, which concedes that the response endpoint in a lipiodol-based comparison is uninterpretable in either direction

The post hoc subgroup analyses point the same way, with conventional chemoembolisation achieving significantly more complete responses in ECOG 0 (p = 0.014) and BCLC A patients (p = 0.027), findings the paper reports without reconciling them against the trend it prefers at 6 months

Survival of patients who became transplantable after downstaging was censored at the day before surgery, so the most successful outcomes in both arms were removed from the survival comparison the trial was powered on

Fewer than a third of patients had unambiguously intermediate-stage disease: 46.3 percent were BCLC A, 26.0 percent were classed BCLC C solely on an ECOG score of 1, and the median largest tumour was 2.6 cm, so the trial did not test beads where their larger drug payload is argued to matter
The reported median survival of 28 and 29 months is explicitly a projection from the 1- and 2-year rates rather than an observed median, since follow-up was a minimum of 2 years

Severe adverse events occurred in 6.2% with a predominantly superselective technique. Differences in patient selection and technique limit comparison with earlier embolisation trials. The within-trial safety findings do not establish equivalence across all settings.

The primary endpoint was two-year survival. Time to progression was secondary. Additional nonrandomised treatments were permitted after chemoembolisation and complicate attribution of later outcomes to the initial embolisation method.

Both arms also differed in the drug delivered (mean 47.2 mg of epirubicin with lipiodol against 57.8 mg of doxorubicin on beads), so the comparison is of two regimens rather than of two delivery systems

CT or MRI was permitted for response assessment. Lipiodol can obscure residual enhancement on CT after conventional TACE, and variation in imaging modality may affect the comparison with drug-eluting beads.

The trial's conclusion that routine use of beads is hard to justify rests on a cost argument of at least 600 euros per treatment rather than on the trial's own data, which cannot exclude a clinically modest difference
24937669.n: 177 of a planned 214 patients with HCC randomised at five Italian centres to conventional chemoembolisation (88) or drug-eluting bead chemoembolisation (89), with a median of two procedures per arm; 46.3 percent were BCLC A, 26.0 percent BCLC C on ECOG 1 alone, and the median largest tumour was 2.6 cm
24937669.bottom_line: PRECISION Italia is the independent test of drug-eluting beads and it was stopped for futility: median time to progression was 9 months in both arms, 2-year survival 56.8 against 55.4 percent (p = 0.949), with less post-procedural pain the only advantage of beads. It cannot establish equivalence, because it was powered for an implausible 20-point survival gain and stopped at 83 percent of its planned size, and nearly half its patients were early-stage with a median tumour under 3 cm.
24937669.funding: No funding source is identified in the article; the authors declare no conflict of interest

limitations: The analysis pools observational and mostly retrospective data, which the authors state limits the ability to control for confounding
Because most included studies did not adjust for known confounders, the authors were forced to use crude measures of association

The authors acknowledge that surgical practice has moved on since the included cohorts, naming laparoscopic resection, reduced clamping and portal vein embolisation, though they argue resection does not lower portal pressure
The investigators excluded grey literature because they judged observational study methods difficult to evaluate from an abstract alone.
critique: The results describe variation in definitions of postoperative decompensation, although all included jaundice and ascites. This limits comparisons across cohorts.
The study’s risk-of-bias assessment classified four of the 11 studies as high risk (QUIPS score 10).

The search began in January 1996, the year the authors’ group first published on this question. Three of the 11 studies came from that group. The discussion interprets the results as supporting international guideline recommendations. This evidence base includes the investigators’ own cohorts.

The decompensation subgroup estimate that drives the recommendation to measure the hepatic venous pressure gradient (pooled OR 14.59, 95% CI 2.81 to 80.06) rests on three studies of 29, 40 and 46 patients, two of them from the authors' unit, and the smallest of the three has perfect separation so its true odds ratio is unbounded

The HVPG-based mortality estimate (OR 8.00, 95% CI 2.59–24.69) comes from Llovet’s 1999 series of 77 patients. Differences between this cohort and larger studies using clinical surrogates prevent a direct comparison of the two measurement strategies.

That comparison is made between subgroups of studies rather than within patients: no included study measured the gradient and the surrogate criteria in the same patients and compared their prognostic performance, so the conclusion that surrogates cannot exclude clinically significant portal hypertension is not something the pooled data can establish

The Results and Supporting Table 3 report that only two of eight survival studies identified portal hypertension as an independent predictor in multivariable analyses. The pooled crude odds ratios cannot separate surgical risk from the underlying severity of cirrhosis.

None of the individual studies reporting operative mortality detected a significant difference by portal hypertension status (11.1% versus 5.1%, 4.6% versus 1.1% and 0.5% versus 0%). These comparisons do not exclude a clinically important difference in perioperative deaths.

Patients with portal hypertension systematically received different operations: anatomical resection in 39 versus 68 percent in the largest study (p < 0.001), 12.1 versus 33.1 percent in another (p = 0.0003), 15.0 versus 31.1 percent in a third (p = 0.001), with less transfusion, so the exposure is confounded with the extent of surgery, and the stratified analysis the authors say addresses this is reported only as data not shown

Several of the sensitivity analyses that support the robustness claim, including the QUIPS low-versus-moderate-to-high comparison and the anatomic-resection strata, are reported as data not shown and cannot be checked

Four different constructs are pooled as one exposure: a gradient of 10 mmHg or more, portal vein pressure of 20 cmH2O or more, the presence of gastro-oesophageal varices, and platelets below 100,000 with a spleen above 12 cm; the prevalence of the resulting exposure ranges from 21.7 to 51.7 percent across studies
No funnel plot, Egger test or any formal assessment of small-study or publication bias is presented, in an analysis whose most extreme subgroup estimates come from its smallest studies

The search covered MEDLINE only, in English only, with no grey literature, no registries and no non-English reports; four full texts could not be obtained and were excluded; only 2 of 11 studies are Asian, and the principal dissenting Asian study was eligible for the survival analysis alone

Giannini’s multicentre ITA.LI.CA cohort of 152 patients found no association with three- or five-year mortality. It was one of two multicentre studies. Ishizawa’s larger series included 386 patients with cirrhosis. The pooled analysis does not establish why the studies differed.

Two of the included studies come from the same unit over overlapping years (1989 to 1997 and 1991 to 1994), and the stated rule against duplicate cohorts is satisfied by entering one into the survival pool and the other into the decompensation pool, which conceals rather than removes the overlap

The senior author disclosed consultancy, grants and other relationships with ten companies. The Discussion cites the group’s own drug-eluting-bead study when considering treatment alternatives. The meta-analysis did not compare resection with those alternatives.
25212123.n: 11 studies with 1,737 patients with cirrhosis and HCC treated surgically; 1,572 patients (574 with and 998 without clinically significant portal hypertension) in the survival analysis with 491 deaths at 3 years and 694 at 5 years, and 1,108 patients (386 with and 722 without) with 197 decompensation events
25212123.bottom_line: Across 11 observational studies of HCC resection, clinically significant portal hypertension was associated with higher odds of three- and five-year mortality (crude OR 2.09 and 2.07) and postoperative decompensation (OR 3.04). In HVPG-defined subgroups, the decompensation estimate (OR 14.59) came from three studies with 115 patients and the mortality estimate (OR 8.00) from one 77-patient series. Confounding by cirrhosis severity limits causal interpretation.
25212123.funding: Supported by Instituto de Salud Carlos III grants PI11/01830 to Bruix and FIS 13/00341 to Bosch, and by FEDER; CIBERehd is funded by the Instituto de Salud Carlos III. Bruix declares consultancy, advisory roles and grants from Bayer and relationships with BioCompatibles, Novartis, Daichi, Arqule, Abbott, Bristol-Myers Squibb, GlaxoSmithKline, Kowa, Lilly and Roche

limitations: Retrospective analysis, although the database was prospectively collected
The risk stratification was never externally validated, only internally cross-validated by 10-fold cross-validation
Surgical indications and tumour burden expanded over the 14-year study period
The authors note that definitions of postoperative liver decompensation vary among studies. Their 19.9% rate should be compared only after considering differences in endpoints and case mix.
The authors attribute the discrepancy between the random-forest variable ranking and the partitioning tree to the difference between the two methods
The authors predict the risk within each class will fall as hepatitis C is cured, so the absolute rates may overstate current risk
critique: In the 20-patient high-risk class, 12 patients developed decompensation and five experienced liver-related mortality over the study period. The percentages (60% and 25%) are imprecise. The tree required at least 20 observations in a node to permit further splitting. That rule does not establish why this node stopped splitting.

The intermediate class holds 297 of 543 patients (54.7 percent) and merges three clinically unlike groups, no portal hypertension with a major resection, portal hypertension with a minor resection, and a minor resection with a MELD above 9, into a single 28.6 percent figure that cannot inform a decision about any of them

The apparent C index was 0.76 (95% CI 0.74–0.79), and the internally cross-validated estimate was 0.78 (0.74–0.82). The intervals overlap. The small difference does not establish how the tree was fitted within each fold or how it would perform externally.

The reported overall error rate of 0.06 is implausible for an outcome with 19.9 percent prevalence, since predicting no decompensation in everyone would err in about 20 percent of cases, and no confusion matrix appears in the main text

The first split, portal hypertension, had OR 2.99 (95% CI 1.93–4.62), the same as its univariable estimate. The hepatectomy split had OR 2.98 (1.97–4.52) without portal hypertension and 2.76 (1.85–4.77) with it. The overall univariable OR for major hepatectomy was 2.98 (1.85–4.77). These estimates describe different groups.

The random-forest importance measure ranks extent of hepatectomy above portal hypertension, reversing the order of the tree on which the paper's conclusion and title rest; the disagreement is instability in the ranking rather than a property of the two methods

The composite decompensation definition drew on Cescon’s 2009 work. Of 108 events, 101 were Clavien–Dindo grade II and 85 of those involved ascites. Thirty-three patients with ascites drained less than 500 mL/day. Postoperative fluid and drain management therefore influence interpretation of this endpoint.

Seventy-three patients with grade 1 liver-related complications were excluded from the endpoint as clinically irrelevant by the operating team, and moving that line turns a 19.9 percent rate into 33.3 percent

The study defined portal hypertension using oesophageal varices or the combination of platelets below 100,000/mm³ and splenic diameter above 120 mm. It did not report HVPG measurement. The tree therefore predicts risk from these clinical findings.

MELD was already dichotomised at greater than 9 in the preoperative analyses. The cohort median was 8 (IQR 7–10). The tree used this cut point in a subgroup undergoing minor resection. External validation is needed before treating 9 as a general decision threshold.

The extent of hepatectomy is a planned-operation variable chosen by surgeons who already knew the patient's portal hypertension status, so the second node partly encodes the team's own risk avoidance: only 20 of the 105 major resections were done in patients with portal hypertension, and those 20 are the high-risk class

Liver-related mortality by risk class (4.4, 9.0 and 25.0 percent) is cumulative over a median 66 months of follow-up and explicitly covers death at any time after surgery, yet it is presented alongside length of stay as though both described the perioperative period; 30-day mortality was zero and in-hospital mortality 0.9 percent

The cohort was deliberately operated beyond guidelines, with 24.9 percent outside Milan criteria, 22.7 percent multifocal, 11.8 percent BCLC B and 4.1 percent BCLC C, and 22.1 percent previously treated, by the same multidisciplinary board that four of the six authors sit on; no measure of tumour burden enters the model at any level

Liver-related mortality in the intermediate class is 27 of 297 (9.0 percent) in the text and 29 in Figure 2, final follow-up is 31 January 2015 in the abstract and 1 January 2015 in the Follow-up section, and the abstract quotes only the cross-validated C index while the Results give a lower apparent value

The study pooled 14 years of surgery at one centre. The operative technique is described as consistent, but indications and tumour burden expanded during the study. Calendar year was not included in the model, so shifts in case mix or perioperative care may affect the estimates.
27248425.n: 543 patients with chronic liver disease who underwent curative resection for HCC at the National Cancer Institute of Milan between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2013; 108 (19.9 percent) developed postoperative liver decompensation and 5 (0.9 percent) died in hospital
27248425.bottom_line: Builds a three-variable decision tree from 543 consecutive resections in which clinical portal hypertension, then extent of hepatectomy, then a MELD above 9 stratify postoperative liver decompensation into 4.9, 28.6 and 60.0 percent. The tree is internally cross-validated only, its high-risk class holds 20 patients, more than half the cohort lands in a single undifferentiated intermediate class, and the endpoint is dominated by grade 2 ascites, so it ranks risk rather than guiding an operation.
27248425.funding: The authors reported institutional support from the Hepato-Oncology Project, 5×1000 and the Italian Association for Cancer Research at the National Cancer Institute in Milan. They reported no conflicts of interest.

limitations: Imaging and survival were censored at transplantation, which the authors defend as the correct method for time to progression while acknowledging it as a limitation
Time to progression was used as a surrogate because survival in this population is confounded by crossover to other therapies
The study was halted on the recommendation of the cancer centre because of accrual difficulties

Of 179 eligible patients, 45 were randomised (25%). The others declined research (43), entered another trial (29), requested Y-90 (49) or requested TACE (13). The authors describe this accrual fraction as encouraging.
The authors state that the Child-Pugh B case mix explains survival lower than expected
critique: The hazard ratio of 0.122 rests on 12 progression events in 45 patients and its confidence interval spans roughly a twentyfold range, so the effect size is not estimable to any useful precision even though the direction is clear

The trial was stopped at 45 of 124 planned patients with no prespecified interim analysis, and the conditional power of 96.8 percent offered in mitigation is a hypothetical calculation assuming the protocol hazard ratio would have held in the 79 patients never enrolled

The arms were unbalanced on precisely the variables that determine progression and survival: half the Y-90 arm was Child-Pugh B at randomisation and 54 percent by the day of first treatment against 24 percent for chemoembolisation, with portal hypertension in 83 against 52 percent (p = 0.051), and no adjustment is made

Time to progression favoured Y-90. Overall survival did not differ significantly. Among listed patients, 13/15 assigned Y-90 and 7/10 assigned conventional TACE received a transplant. These descriptive counts do not establish a reduction in waitlist dropout.

Censoring at transplantation removes the most favourable outcomes from both arms, and with most patients listed for transplantation the proportion censored is large, which is why competing-risk and inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted analyses were needed to support the primary result

Enrolment was 25 percent of eligible patients at a single centre, with 49 requesting Y-90 and 13 requesting chemoembolisation outside the trial, so the randomised cohort is the minority indifferent between the two at a centre with a strong radioembolisation programme
Two of 21 chemoembolisation patients were treated off study, so the control arm as delivered is smaller still

Y-90 patients waited longer for their first treatment than chemoembolisation patients, which the authors present as a strength but which also means the two arms differ in the interval between staging and treatment

Three authors including the senior author advise the manufacturer of the device tested, and the trial's conclusion prompted the centre to change its own practice to radioembolisation for transplant bridging
The paper is universally cited as PREMIERE although it never uses that name, which makes its small size and single-centre origin easy to overlook
27575820.n: At one US centre, 179 eligible patients with BCLC A or B HCC unsuitable for resection or ablation were screened between October 2009 and October 2015. The last enrolment was 14 July 2015. Forty-five were randomised to Y-90 glass microspheres (24, planned 120 Gy) or conventional TACE (21). Most were listed for transplant and half the Y-90 arm had Child-Pugh B liver function.
27575820.bottom_line: Widely cited as PREMIERE, this is a 45-patient single-centre randomised trial in which radioembolisation gave a much longer time to progression than chemoembolisation (median over 26 against 6.8 months, HR 0.122) with identical survival. It was stopped for slow accrual at a third of its planned size with no prespecified interim analysis, the endpoint is a surrogate censored at transplantation, and the arms were poorly balanced on liver function.
27575820.funding: Funded in part by NIH grant CA126809; three authors, including the senior author, advise BTG International, which manufactures the TheraSphere device tested

limitations: The trial enrolled only patients who progressed during sorafenib treatment, so the authors state that no firm conclusion can be drawn about regorafenib in patients who do not tolerate sorafenib
Special populations such as patients co-infected with HIV were not included

The authors note that the association between adverse events such as hand-foot skin reaction and outcome is based on post-randomisation events and so cannot be used to select patients likely to benefit
critique: Eligibility required documented tolerance of sorafenib before progression on it, which selects for tolerance of a related multikinase inhibitor as well, so the 10.6-month median and the manageable toxicity profile describe a population pre-selected on the exposure being tested

The trial's own health-related quality-of-life results favoured placebo: FACT-Hep and the Trial Outcome Index were significantly worse with regorafenib (p = 0.0006 and p < 0.0001), and the authors set this aside on the grounds that published minimally important difference thresholds were not met, with the data placed in an appendix

Every treated patient had an adverse event and 47 of 379 regorafenib patients discontinued for an adverse event unrelated to disease progression against 12 of 194 on placebo, so the 2.8-month median gain is bought at a cost the trial measured but discounted

Investigators assessed response and progression by mRECIST and RECIST without blinded independent central review. Both complete responses by mRECIST, which measures viable enhancing tumour, also met EASL complete-response criteria.

Patients who progressed from Child-Pugh A to B between screening and randomisation were enrolled, disclosed only in a footnote to the baseline table, and 5 regorafenib and 6 placebo patients were Child-Pugh B at baseline
Asian recruitment was capped at 40 percent by design, which constrains the trial's representativeness of the global disease by administrative fiat rather than by eligibility

Pharmacokinetic and biomarker evaluations are stated not to be reported here, so the trial that established sorafenib-to-regorafenib sequencing published no biomarker that would identify who should receive it

The comparator is placebo plus best supportive care, appropriate when the trial was designed but no longer the relevant control, and the trial cannot speak to regorafenib after an immunotherapy combination, which is now the usual first line

Of 843 screened patients, 270 were not randomised, including 238 screening failures. The report does not characterise this excluded population. The trial applies to eligible patients who progressed after tolerating sorafenib.

The Discussion's claim that prolonging exposure to multikinase inhibitors in sequence extends survival cannot be separated from the selection the eligibility criteria imposed, since only patients who had already demonstrated tolerance and a reasonable duration on sorafenib could enter

All statistical analyses were performed by the funder, which also provided the drug, co-designed the trial, collected and interpreted the data, prepared the report and paid for the writing assistance, so no analysis independent of Bayer underlies the registration result
27932229.n: 573 of 843 screened patients with HCC, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0 or 1 who had tolerated sorafenib and progressed on it, randomised 2:1 to regorafenib (379) or placebo (194) between May 2013 and December 2015, with Asian recruitment capped at 40 percent; median prior sorafenib duration 7.8 months in both arms
27932229.bottom_line: RESORCE showed a survival benefit for regorafenib after sorafenib in patients who had tolerated sorafenib: median overall survival 10.6 vs 7.8 months (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50–0.79). Progression-free survival, time to progression and response also favoured regorafenib. Every treated regorafenib recipient had an adverse event. FACT-Hep Total and Trial Outcome Index scores were statistically lower, but the differences fell below established thresholds of clinical importance.
27932229.funding: Funded by Bayer, which provided the study drug, designed the trial with the principal investigator and steering committee, took part in data collection and interpretation and in preparing the report, performed all statistical analyses and funded writing assistance; three authors are Bayer employees, one holding stock, and the principal investigator reports grants and personal fees from Bayer

limitations: More patients assigned radioembolisation than sorafenib never received their allocated treatment, which the authors state
There was a long work-up delay before radioembolisation
Many participating centres had limited experience with radioembolisation despite certification requirements
Dose-related efficacy had not been evaluated at the time of the report, which the authors list as a limitation
critique: Of 237 assigned radioembolisation, 53 did not receive it and 26 of those received sorafenib. Both the ITT comparison (HR 1.15) and the per-protocol comparison (median OS 9.9 vs 9.9 months, HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.79–1.24) failed to show a survival advantage as delivered in SARAH.

Activity was prescribed by body surface area. Tumour dosimetry was a secondary endpoint reported separately. In 121 patients with evaluable dose data, median OS was 14.1 months with tumour dose ≥100 Gy vs 6.1 months below 100 Gy. Dose was not randomised, so this association does not establish a dose effect or explain the trial result (Hermann et al., PMID 32602828).

Macrovascular invasion was present in about 60% overall (63% of the radioembolisation arm), 16% had Child-Pugh B7 liver function, and median tumour burden was 18% of liver volume. In an exploratory subset with burden ≤25% and ALBI grade 1, median OS was 21.9 vs 17.0 months (37 vs 48 patients, HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.44–1.21, p=0.22). This was a separate post hoc analysis (PMID 31797680).

The operational penalty fell entirely on one arm: a median 29 days from randomisation to radioembolisation against 7 days to sorafenib in a population whose median survival was about 9 months, so roughly a tenth of the available survival time was consumed by work-up in the experimental arm alone

Randomisation was stratified by centre, ECOG status, prior TACE and macrovascular invasion. Entry category itself was not a stratum. The exploratory OS HR was 0.98 after unsuccessful TACE vs 1.31 without it (interaction p=0.14). These data do not establish different effects by entry category.
The comparator is now historical, so the trial cannot say how radioembolisation performs against the immunotherapy doublets that have replaced sorafenib in first-line advanced disease

Quality of life and tolerability favoured radioembolisation, which in an open-label trial with a single procedure against a continuously dosed oral drug reflects the shape of the two treatments as much as their toxicity
Serious adverse events occurred in 176/216 sorafenib recipients (81.5%). The 81% and 82% values in different parts of the report refer to the same patients.

Assistance Publique–Hôpitaux de Paris was the academic sponsor. Device manufacturer Sirtex funded the trial and editorial assistance. The report states that neither sponsor nor funder had a role in design, collection, analysis or interpretation. The coordinating investigator disclosed Sirtex grants and personal fees.
29107679.n: At 25 French centres, 467 patients were randomised and 459 analysed (237 assigned Y-90 resin radioembolisation, 222 sorafenib). Entry included BCLC C HCC, unresectable recurrence after curative treatment or progression after two TACE treatments. Macrovascular invasion was present in about 60% overall (63% in the radioembolisation arm), 16% had Child-Pugh B7 liver function, and 22% assigned radioembolisation never received it.
29107679.bottom_line: SARAH found no overall survival advantage for radioembolisation over sorafenib (ITT median 8.0 vs 9.9 months, HR 1.15). Tolerability and quality of life favoured radioembolisation. Although 22% assigned radioembolisation did not receive it, the per-protocol comparison was also null (9.9 vs 9.9 months, HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.79–1.24). The trial used body-surface-area dosing. A subsequent observational analysis linked higher tumour dose with longer survival but cannot establish a causal dose effect (PMID 32602828).
29107679.funding: Funded by Sirtex Medical, which makes the resin microspheres tested, and which also paid for editorial assistance

limitations: A high proportion of patients assigned radioembolisation never received it, which the authors list first
The EQ-5D instrument used for quality of life is not liver-specific
The BCLC C survival finding rests on a small sample and was not corrected for multiplicity, so the authors state it should be considered exploratory

The authors note that patients from five of the eleven participating countries had to travel to Singapore for work-up and treatment and then return home for follow-up, which caused progression, death and consent withdrawal before treatment
critique: The primary comparison is partly a test of logistics rather than of biology: 52 of 182 patients assigned radioembolisation never received it, 29 of them because they were found ineligible after randomisation, and all remained in the intention-to-treat analysis, while the median interval from randomisation to treatment was 21 days for radioembolisation against 3 days for sorafenib in a population surviving about 9 months

Favourable progression-free survival, time to progression, 6-month survival and BCLC C survival results were confined to treated-patient analyses. Treatment receipt selected for patients who remained fit and anatomically suitable. By ITT, tumour response and toxicity-time measures favoured radioembolisation.

SIRveNIB allowed one radioembolisation, whereas SARAH allowed repeat treatment. Activity in SIRveNIB was calculated by body surface area or an individualised partition model. The protocol did not specify a tumour-absorbed-dose target, and the trial cannot establish that patients received an inadequate dose.
Cross-border delivery of the intervention was built into the design, so the treatment arm carried an operational burden that no routine practice would impose and that the control arm did not share

SIRveNIB tested superiority against sorafenib and found no significant overall survival advantage. It did not establish equivalence or directly compare radioembolisation with current first-line immunotherapy combinations.

The trial is described as a two-tailed superiority-or-detriment design, so a null result cannot be read as equivalence, yet the conclusion that overall survival did not differ is routinely cited as though it established that
Randomisation was stratified by centre and portal vein thrombosis. The study spanned 11 countries and did not report a separate analysis of travel requirements or cross-border treatment delays.

For 6-month survival in treated patients, Table 2 reports 81.5% (95% CI 74.7–88.4) with radioembolisation vs 68.0% (60.7–75.3) with sorafenib, difference 13.5 percentage points (3.5–23.6). The Results sentence prints 81.0% and misassigns the confidence intervals.
Eighteen of 40 authors disclosed Sirtex research funding. The lead author reported speaker and advisory roles, and the manuscript received Sirtex-supported editorial assistance.
29498924.n: 360 patients with BCLC B or C HCC confined to the liver, not amenable to curative treatment, randomised 1:1 at 27 centres in 11 Asia-Pacific countries between July 2010 and May 2016 to a single Y-90 resin radioembolisation (182) or sorafenib (178); 90 percent were Child-Pugh A and about 30 percent had portal vein thrombosis, and only 130 of 182 assigned radioembolisation received it
29498924.bottom_line: In SIRveNIB, median overall survival by ITT was 8.8 months with Y-90 radioembolisation and 10.0 with sorafenib, without a significant difference. Tumour response favoured radioembolisation (16.5% vs 1.7%, p<0.001), as did toxicity-time measures. Assigned treatment was never received by 28.6% vs 9.0%. Favourable survival or progression comparisons in the treated population are susceptible to post-randomisation selection.
29498924.funding: Funding and disclosures. Sirtex Medical, manufacturer of the resin microspheres, supported this investigator-initiated study and language editing. The lead author disclosed honoraria, consultancy, speakers bureau membership and institutional research funding. Eighteen of 40 authors disclosed Sirtex research funding.

limitations: All microwave ablations used a single device (Acculis Sulis VpMTA) when many commercially available systems differ in antenna design, frequency, probe number and power, so the result does not generalise across devices
Patients were excluded after randomisation for not receiving the allocated intervention or for immediate loss to follow-up, which forced a per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat analysis
Allocation used sealed opaque envelopes, which the authors call a non-optimal method of concealment and masking, and operators were not masked

The design assumed 2.7 percent local progression with microwave and 15.4 percent with radiofrequency ablation, which the authors concede was optimistic; the observed difference was much smaller than estimated
Only 11 lesions measured 3 to 4 cm, so the larger-lesion analysis in which microwave ablation might differ was not possible
Two years is short follow-up for BCLC 0 to A disease, and management after local tumour progression was not assessed in this report
The authors state that equivalence of the two techniques cannot be confirmed from a trial designed to assess superiority
critique: Patients were randomised, whereas the primary endpoint counted lesions. Two or three lesions were present in 24/68 and 26/72 patients (about 35% overall). No adjustment for within-patient correlation was described, which can make lesion-level estimates appear more precise.

The trial had almost no power for the difference actually seen: 78 lesions per arm were sized for a 12.7 percentage-point absolute gap, while the observed gap was 6 percentage points, so the p value of 0.27 is uninformative rather than reassuring, yet the Interpretation is written as a positive statement that progression was low with both methods

Nine lesions with residual unablated tumour at one month were treated again. They remained in the primary denominators, but follow-up for local progression started when complete ablation was documented.

The Methods justify using a raw proportion rather than a Kaplan-Meier estimate on the grounds that all lesions were assessable at 2 years, but the at-risk table under the progression figure shows only 44 radiofrequency and 52 microwave lesions at risk at 2 years with 48 and 41 censored, so the stated assumption is contradicted by the published figure

The printed captions of Figures 2 and 3 appear transposed. The plotted log-rank p values of 0.1854 and 0.8012 concern different outcomes. For overall survival, the text gives p=0.87 and the plot p=0.8012. Both are nonsignificant.

The report prints mean ablation-zone volumes as 5.4 mm³ (SD 20.8) with microwave and 28.4 mm³ (SD 21) with radiofrequency (p=0.35). The units and the wide microwave dispersion make these volume values difficult to interpret.

Baseline distribution of lesions differed between arms in ways that bear on ablation difficulty and heat-sink: segment II held 18 microwave versus 5 radiofrequency lesions, the right lobe 54 versus 66, and Child-Pugh B patients were 20 versus 27 percent; no adjustment or sensitivity analysis is reported

New distant intrahepatic foci appeared in 72 and 70 percent of lesions by 2 years and 13 to 16 percent of patients were transplanted and censored, so the primary endpoint was measured against a background in which nearly every patient developed new disease, and local progression cannot separate technique quality from tumour biology

ClinicalTrials.gov first posted NCT02859753 on 9 August 2016, after enrolment ended in February 2015. The authors report university registration in 2011, but the public registry does not independently establish the analysis plan at enrolment.

The five operators had 8 to 20 years of interventional oncology experience, but radiofrequency ablation was the established technique and microwave the newer one during 2011 to 2015; an operator learning curve favouring the control arm is neither measured nor discussed

The reported risk ratio of 1.62 is oriented with radiofrequency ablation as the numerator while the point estimate favours microwave ablation, and the paper never states the direction, so the only effect estimate in the abstract reads as if it disfavoured the experimental arm

The trial was funded by Microsulis (AngioDynamics), maker of the microwave device, the sponsor reviewed the manuscript, and the editing support was paid for from the same grant, yet the declaration of interests reads in full that the authors have no competing interests
29503247.n: 152 patients with BCLC 0 or A HCC of 4 cm or smaller randomised at four French and Swiss centres; 144 analysed per protocol, 71 patients with 98 lesions treated by microwave ablation and 73 with 104 lesions by radiofrequency ablation
29503247.bottom_line: At 2 years, local tumour progression affected 6/98 lesions with microwave ablation and 12/104 with radiofrequency ablation (reported RR 1.62, 95% CI 0.66–3.94, p=0.27). The trial did not demonstrate superiority or establish equivalence. Residual tumour, time to progression, survival and complications did not differ significantly. The post hoc 3–4 cm subgroup included only 11 lesions.
29503247.funding: Grant from Microsulis (AngioDynamics), the manufacturer of the microwave device, which also funded editing support; the sponsor reviewed the submitted manuscript; the authors declare no competing interests

limitations: Open-label design without blinded response assessment, which the authors state was not feasible because imaging appearances differ after the two treatments
A hepatitis B-predominant population, which the authors acknowledge limits generalisability
critique: Median time to progression with sorafenib was 11.7 weeks, shorter than in the pivotal sorafenib trials. Overall survival was comparable to SHARP. Hepatitis B accounted for 84.4% of this cohort. Cross-trial differences cannot establish control-arm underperformance.

Overall survival is a secondary endpoint whose upper confidence limit reaches 0.98, and 90.7 percent of the sorafenib arm crossed over to chemoembolisation plus radiotherapy within 24 weeks, so the survival comparison contrasts immediate with deferred locoregional therapy rather than two treatments

The primary endpoint was PFS at 12 weeks, assessed by an independent radiologist at the trial centre who knew treatment allocation. A separate blinded review at the end of the study found 4.8% discordance. The treatment-specific imaging appearances could still affect assessment.

The proportion of patients with cirrhosis is never reported, which is the variable that determines whether repeated chemoembolisation plus 45 Gy is safe in another unit's hands, as the accompanying commentary points out

The protocol is hard to export: cisplatin-based chemoembolisation on a fixed 6-week schedule with gelatin sponge omitted at operator discretion, a median of four sessions in 24 weeks, and a median of 40 Gy in 2.5 to 3.0 Gy fractions by 3D-conformal technique rather than contemporary stereotactic radiotherapy

The intervention is a two-component regimen and the trial cannot say what each contributes, so the result cannot be read as evidence for radiotherapy or for chemoembolisation separately in portal vein invasion

Ninety patients at one centre in a population with a median tumour of 9.7 cm and multifocal disease in 79 percent is too small to support the aggressive strategy the trial advocates for patients whose liver is already heavily burdened
The comparator is no longer first-line, so the trial cannot address whether this regimen should be added to or substituted for an immunotherapy combination in macrovascular invasion

Patients with main portal vein invasion and preserved flow only on one side were eligible, so the irradiated volume and the embolised territory varied with anatomy in ways the paper does not relate to outcome
29543938.n: 90 treatment-naive patients with liver-confined HCC invading at least the first- or second-branch portal vein with preserved unilateral portal flow, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0 to 1, randomised 1:1 at Asan Medical Center, Seoul between July 2013 and October 2016 to sorafenib (45) or chemoembolisation every 6 weeks plus 3D-conformal radiotherapy to the vascular invasion (45); median maximal tumour diameter was 9.7 cm, 78.9 percent had multiple lesions and 84.4 percent had hepatitis B
29543938.bottom_line: At a single centre, TACE plus conformal radiotherapy improved 12-week PFS (86.7% vs 34.3%) and median OS (55.0 vs 43.0 weeks) compared with sorafenib for HCC with macroscopic vascular invasion. The primary imaging reader was independent but unblinded. An end-of-study blinded central review found 4.8% discordance. Crossover from sorafenib reached 90.7% by 24 weeks. Sorafenib time to progression was shorter than in pivotal trials, but OS was comparable to SHARP.
29543938.funding: Publicly and institutionally funded; one author declares advisory and research funding from Bayer, the manufacturer of the comparator drug, and from Gilead

limitations: Patients with Child-Pugh class B or worse liver function and poorer performance status were excluded, and the authors state that further studies are needed to establish safety and efficacy in them

The authors report that the hazard ratio for death was 0.69 in hepatitis B-related and 1.11 in hepatitis C-related disease, and 0.86 in patients of Asian race but 1.01 in patients enrolled in Asia, and state that further analyses are needed to understand these differences

The authors note that hazard ratios in subgroups can be distorted by small numbers, imbalances in prognostic factors or differences in subsequent therapy, and that subgroup confidence intervals are descriptive with no adjustment for multiplicity
Most cabozantinib recipients required a dose reduction. The median average daily dose was 35.8 mg, which the authors described as similar to the 43 mg delivered in a renal-cell carcinoma trial.
The authors state that the population studied represents a small percentage of patients with HCC
critique: The intention-to-treat population is defined by a data cutoff rather than by randomisation: 773 patients were randomised by September 2017 but only the 707 randomised before 1 June 2017 are analysed, so 66 randomised patients appear in no efficacy analysis of a trial described as intention to treat

The effect estimate shrank between the two looks, from a hazard ratio of 0.71 at 321 deaths to 0.76 at 484 deaths, which is the expected pattern when a trial is stopped at the first boundary crossing and means the published 0.76 is more likely an overestimate than an underestimate of the true effect

The protocol specified that no further analysis of overall survival would be performed once the null was rejected at an interim look, so the trial was designed in a way that guarantees the prespecified final estimate at 621 deaths can never exist

Placebo median progression-free survival was 1.9 months with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.9 to 1.9, which is the first scheduled 8-week scan, so the progression-free survival hazard ratio of 0.44 is substantially an artefact of the assessment schedule rather than a measure of disease control

Progression and response were assessed by the investigator with no blinded independent central review, and an objective response rate of 4 percent (18 partial responses) against under 1 percent means the progression-free survival advantage consists almost entirely of stable disease on serial imaging
The subgroup whose only previous therapy was sorafenib, with a hazard ratio of 0.70, is the figure quoted in practice, and the paper states it was not among the prespecified subgroup analyses

Treatment-related grade 5 events occurred in 6 cabozantinib patients (hepatic failure, bronchoesophageal fistula, portal vein thrombosis, upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage, pulmonary embolism and hepatorenal syndrome) against 1 on placebo, so roughly 1.3 percent of patients died of the drug against a 2.2-month median gain

Health-related quality of life, pharmacokinetic and biomarker analyses are all stated not to be reported here, so in a drug whose principal cost is toxicity the patient-reported outcomes were withheld from the publication that established its use

Cabozantinib targets VEGF receptors as well as MET and AXL. CELESTIAL neither selected nor stratified patients by MET or AXL and did not establish either as a predictor of benefit. The negative MET-selected tivantinib trial concerned a different drug.

After discontinuation, 26% of the cabozantinib group and 33% of the placebo group received subsequent systemic or local anticancer treatment, excluding radiotherapy. The comparison was against placebo rather than another active systemic regimen.

Aetiology, a stratification factor, was recorded from case-report forms with 16 to 20 percent unknown and alcohol-related disease imbalanced at 24 against 16 percent, so the factor used to balance the randomisation was itself imprecisely captured
One patient with ECOG performance status 2 was randomised despite the eligibility requirement of 0 or 1, acknowledged only in a footnote to the baseline table

Exelixis collected and analysed the data in collaboration with the academic authors and provided medical writing and editorial support. The authors reported access to the data. The publication does not describe a separate independent statistical replication.
29972759.n: 707 patients with advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0 or 1, who had progressed after at least one systemic therapy including sorafenib, randomised 2:1 at 95 centres in 19 countries and included in the 1 June 2017 interim analysis; 773 were randomised in all by September 2017, and 27 percent of those analysed had received two prior systemic regimens
29972759.bottom_line: In previously sorafenib-treated advanced HCC, cabozantinib improved median overall survival from 8.0 to 10.2 months versus placebo (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63–0.92, P = 0.005) and progression-free survival from 1.9 to 5.2 months. The second of two planned interim analyses crossed the efficacy boundary at 78% of the deaths planned for the final analysis. Objective response was 4% with cabozantinib. Grade 3–4 adverse events of any cause occurred in 68% versus 36%. The median average daily cabozantinib dose was 35.8 mg, from a 60 mg starting dose.
29972759.funding: Funded by Exelixis, which designed the trial with the first and last authors, was responsible with them for data collection and analysis, collaborated on the first draft and provided medical writing and editorial assistance; three authors are Exelixis employees holding company stock, and most academic authors report industry consultancy or advisory fees

limitations: Patients with Child-Pugh class B or worse cirrhosis were excluded in line with guideline recommendations for trial exclusion
Patients with an alpha-fetoprotein below 400 ng/mL were excluded on the basis of the earlier REACH result, so no further data exist for them
Only sorafenib-pretreated patients were enrolled, which the authors list as a limitation, with an expansion cohort initiated for patients given other first-line treatments
Baseline alpha-fetoprotein was the only factor with a potential imbalance between groups, which the authors attribute to chance
Health-related quality of life, pharmacokinetic and immunogenicity results are stated to be reported separately
critique: A protocol amendment on 24 April 2017, nearly two years into enrolment, removed the planned interim efficacy analysis and cut the required sample from 399 to 279 patients while reducing the assumed hazard ratio, a decision taken by the principal investigator, the steering committee and the sponsor together, and the final analysis then occurred at exactly the 221 deaths the revised design required

Observed placebo median survival was 7.3 months vs 4.5 months assumed in the design. The authors discussed lower baseline AFP in the placebo arm as a possible contributor and estimated a placebo median of 6.7 months after adjustment. Neither comparison replaces the randomised overall survival estimate.

Baseline AFP was higher with ramucirumab (median 3,920 ng/mL) than with placebo (2,741 ng/mL), an imbalance favouring placebo. AFP was not a stratification factor. A post hoc AFP-adjusted analysis still significantly favoured ramucirumab. The placebo upper quartile is 11,681 in Table 1 and 11,861 in the text.

The absolute median gain is 1.2 months with an objective response rate of about 5 percent, so the benefit rests on a time-to-event endpoint in a population whose median survival remains under 9 months

The 400 ng/mL threshold is carried over from a subgroup of the negative REACH trial with no stated biological derivation, and the paper reports no VEGFR2 or other mechanistic marker linking ramucirumab's target to the benefit, so the selection is prognostic enrichment rather than demonstrated prediction

Pooling REACH-2 with the AFP-selected REACH subgroup gave OS HR 0.689 (95% CI 0.568–0.835) in the frailty model and HR 0.694 in the stratified analysis. The pooled estimate incorporates the subgroup that generated the hypothesis and therefore cannot serve as independent replication.
Response and progression were assessed locally by investigators under RECIST 1.1 with no blinded independent central review
Median follow-up was 7.6 months. Approximately 76% of participants had died by the analysis cutoff, providing substantial event information for the overall survival estimate.

Time to deterioration of the eight-item FHSI symptom score was 3.7 months with ramucirumab vs 2.8 with placebo (HR 0.799, 95% CI 0.545–1.171, p=0.238). This fourth endpoint in the testing sequence did not differ significantly. Broader quality-of-life results were deferred to a separate report.

The funder reported roles in study design and data collection and involvement in analysis, interpretation and writing. Two authors reported employment, shareholdings and pending patents with Eli Lilly.

In REACH-2, grade ≥3 hypertension occurred in 13% with ramucirumab vs 5% with placebo, and grade ≥3 hyponatraemia in 6% vs 0%. These trial-specific safety estimates should be distinguished from the pooled REACH/REACH-2 rates.
30665869.n: 292 of 436 screened patients with advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A and a baseline alpha-fetoprotein of 400 ng/mL or more who had previously received sorafenib, randomised 2:1 to ramucirumab (197) or placebo (95) between July 2015 and August 2017; 50 patients (17 percent) had stopped sorafenib for intolerance and median prior sorafenib duration was 4.1 months
30665869.bottom_line: REACH-2 was the first positive biomarker-selected phase 3 HCC trial. After sorafenib in patients with AFP ≥400 ng/mL, median overall survival was 8.5 months with ramucirumab and 7.3 with placebo (HR 0.710, 95% CI 0.531–0.949, p=0.0199). Response with ramucirumab was 5%. Sample size and the assumed effect changed during enrolment. Baseline AFP favoured placebo, and a post hoc AFP-adjusted analysis still favoured ramucirumab.
30665869.funding: Funded by Eli Lilly, which had roles in the design of both REACH and REACH-2 and in data collection, analysis, interpretation and writing of the report; two authors are Lilly employees, shareholders and hold pending patents

limitations: Single institution with an open-label design, which the authors acknowledge leaves residual bias
The subgroup analyses were not adjusted for multiple testing and may be false-positive, as the authors state
Nearly all patients had hepatitis B-related disease, which the authors note limits generalisability
Repeat hepatectomy was open, and the authors call for a comparison against laparoscopic repeat hepatectomy, which has not been studied
critique: The study classified time to recurrence (≤12 vs >12 months) in a subgroup analysis. This timing alone cannot distinguish intrahepatic metastasis from a new primary HCC.

The trial was powered against a surgical result that did not exist: the calculation assumed 5-year survival of 56 percent after repeat hepatectomy and 39 percent after ablation, and the observed figures were 43.6 and 38.5 percent, so the ablation assumption was accurate and the surgical one was 12 points too optimistic

The Key Points correctly report no statistically significant difference in overall survival. With HR 1.26 (95% CI 0.91–1.76), the superiority trial leaves clinically important differences compatible with its data. It did not test equivalence.

The primary endpoint is analysed six times in different populations (intention to treat p = 0.17, excluding additional anticancer treatment p = 0.24, minor hepatectomy only p = 0.20, per protocol p = 0.10, and z tests on the 5-year rates p = 0.291 and p = 0.25) with no hierarchy or multiplicity control stated

The main Results report 5-year repeat recurrence-free survival of 36.4% vs 28.2% in the per-protocol analysis (p=0.04), whereas the ITT comparison gave p=0.09. Exclusion of crossovers and patients lost to follow-up changes the population. Local repeat recurrence and early repeat recurrence also had p=0.04.

Subgroup variables came from the trial’s multivariable prognostic model. There were 81/240 patients with a nodule >3 cm, 96 with AFP >200 ng/mL and 50 with multifocal disease. No interaction test was reported. The subgroup forest plot was corrected in January 2020. These exploratory associations need confirmation.

Eligibility excluded any nodule within 1.0 cm of the gastrointestinal tract, hilum, cava, main hepatic veins, gallbladder or diaphragm, which removes every location in which ablation is known to fail, and ablation still produced nearly twice the local recurrence in that favourable anatomy

Both arms worked to a 0.5 cm margin standard, below the margin usually recommended for either technique, and 99 of 120 surgical patients had less than a bisegmentectomy, so the surgical arm is mostly limited open resection rather than anatomical re-resection

Safety is analysed as treated on 116 surgical and 124 ablation patients, different denominators from the efficacy analysis, and the surgical safety group contains one patient who received only intraoperative ablation and two who had resection plus intratumoral ethanol

Grade 3 or 4 complications were 6.0 against 1.6 percent with p = 0.09, so the severe-complication difference is not significant and the headline 22.4 against 7.3 percent is driven by Clavien-Dindo grade 1 and 2 events that the abstract reports only as a composite

The cohort is narrow in ways that remove the patients for whom the question is hardest: age capped at 60 with a median of 53, Child-Pugh A with no varices or ascites, platelets above 50 and prothrombin prolongation under 5 seconds, 90 percent male and almost entirely hepatitis B

Local repeat recurrence meant new disease within 1 cm of the ablation zone or resection margin. Surveillance included ultrasound and AFP every 2 months during the first 2 years and contrast-enhanced CT or MRI every 4–6 months. Early recurrence was defined as within 12 months.

Recurrence after treatment was managed at clinician discretion and 38 of 73 surgical and 51 of 77 ablation patients received multidisciplinary salvage, so overall survival reflects an unrandomised salvage pathway that was used more often in the ablation arm

All patients had undergone an R0 resection without residual disease at 2 months. The trial therefore compared two treatments among patients previously fit for surgery. Salvage transplantation is mentioned in the Introduction but was not a trial arm.

The study was conducted at a high-volume Chinese liver surgery centre. Repeat hepatectomy had a 22.4% complication rate, no perioperative deaths and a median 8-day hospital stay. Applicability depends on patient selection and local surgical experience.
31774468.n: 240 of 518 screened patients aged 20 to 60 with early-stage recurrent HCC after a previous R0 resection (solitary nodule 5 cm or less, or up to 3 nodules each 3 cm or less), randomised 1:1 at the Eastern Hepatobiliary Surgery Hospital in Shanghai between June 2010 and January 2013; 216 of 240 (90 percent) were men and 217 completed the trial
31774468.bottom_line: In Xia et al., 5-year overall survival after repeat resection vs percutaneous RFA for recurrent HCC was 43.6% vs 38.5% (HR for death with RFA 1.26, 95% CI 0.91–1.76, p=0.17). Local repeat recurrence was 21.7% vs 37.8%, and complications were 22.4% vs 7.3%. The size >3 cm and AFP >200 ng/mL subgroups had 81 and 96 patients, respectively. Subgroup comparisons were exploratory, and eligibility excluded anatomically difficult ablation sites.
31774468.funding: Government-funded; the authors declare no conflicts of interest

limitations: Open-label design, chosen to spare patients two placebo infusions, which the authors list as a limitation although blinded independent review protected the progression-free survival endpoint
Eligibility required Child-Pugh A liver function, screening endoscopy and treatment of varices as clinically indicated. Safety in patients outside these criteria requires separate evidence.
The authors note that no biomarker has been shown to predict benefit in HCC and that work is needed to identify who benefits
critique: Median overall survival had not been reached in the combination arm at the primary analysis. The 2022 update describes that earlier estimate as immature and reports survival after longer follow-up.

The primary survival analysis is the first interim look at 161 of 312 planned deaths (52 percent) with a median follow-up of 8.6 months, and the 12-month landmark survival rates of 67.2 and 54.6 percent are therefore estimated beyond the median duration of follow-up in either arm

Dose modification was not permitted for atezolizumab or bevacizumab but was permitted for sorafenib, and patients who stopped one component of the combination could continue the other, so the experimental regimen was a flexible strategy while the control was a fixed comparator, and attrition for toxicity falls differently in the two arms by design
Both arms could continue treatment beyond radiographic progression at the investigator's judgment of clinical benefit, a decision made without masking in a trial whose primary endpoint is survival

The 2:1 allocation leaves 165 control patients with 65 deaths, so every comparison rests on an imprecisely estimated sorafenib arm, and the stratified analyses dropped ECOG performance status from the stratification factors used in analysis despite its being a randomisation stratum, with no explanation

Screening endoscopy and management of varices as needed were required before enrolment. Untreated or incompletely treated varices with bleeding or high bleeding risk were excluded. About 26% had varices and 11–14% received prior variceal treatment. The reported bleeding rates apply to this screened population.
Diagnosis could be made on clinical and imaging criteria without tissue, and 2 to 4 percent of patients were BCLC stage A, so a minority of a first-line systemic therapy trial had early-stage disease

Patient-reported quality of life, physical functioning and role functioning were secondary endpoints defined on a 10-point EORTC change and collected by self-report in an unmasked trial, which is the circumstance in which such endpoints are least interpretable

No biomarker selection or biomarker result is reported although atezolizumab is a PD-L1 inhibitor with companion diagnostics in other tumours, so there is no way to identify the roughly one patient in four who responds

Overall 240/501 patients (48%) had HBV, 153/501 (31%) had nonviral disease and about 40% came from Asia excluding Japan.
